title: Retry: replay last 50 accepted readings and hold over 10% refused
summary: Retry of job 20261028-055601-hg0n, which ended failed with no verification only because free disk was 9.8 GB against the 10 GB required before the verifier (an environment failure, not a finding on the work). The work is the same as the accepted reading: an `athena check-reading` subcommand, plus a replay of the newest 50 accepted readings through the base and candidate builds, stored as a typed record, shown to the verifier, and holding the job if more than 10% are newly refused. Audience: maintainers and the verifier. The disk-cleanup fix in the introspection is a separate job and is not done here.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for each behavior and fmt, clippy and test criteria.
Behavior criteria name cargo commands the verifier can run.
Criteria check the held-or-not outcome of the replay, not that wiring exists.
An empty history yields 'no replay: <reason>', not a pass.
The 10% hold is enforced in code with a constant.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Job 20261028-055601-hg0n's one recorded outcome reason (low disk before the verifier) is addressed by retrying on the same scope; it no longer applies to the work, and the operator frees disk before the retry.
The typed request takes precedence over the introspection's proposed disk-reclaim request, so automatic disk cleanup is out of scope and stays a separate job.
The earlier job 20261028-034820-v3rf failed because its plan wrote an unaccepted replay.md; this retry stores the result as a typed record and creates no replay.md.
The replay input is the newest 50 requests that have accepted readings in records; tests use fixture records.
The 10% threshold is a code constant, not config.
The test override sits in front of tree resolution and the subcommand probe; the no-model-call check compares model call counts with and without a candidate change, with no skip switch.

acceptance_criteria.text: `athena check-reading` takes a stored request and reading and prints accept or refuse with the reason, using the same acceptance rules as reading.rs; a fixture test shows both outputs (cargo test -p athena-cli).
A test builds a candidate-like rule change over fixture records and lists the newly refused requests (refused by candidate, accepted by base) with the count (cargo test -p athena-core).
A test shows the replay uses only the newest 50 requests that have accepted readings, and that an empty history gives 'no replay: <reason>', not a pass (cargo test -p athena-core).

A test shows more than 10% newly refused is held with the list, exactly 10% or less is not held, and a candidate whose criteria intend a higher rate is not held, with the replay still recorded (cargo test -p athena-core).

A pipeline test, with the override in front of tree resolution and the subcommand probe, holds a candidate over the threshold (Rejected, not landed); the typed replay record and the Athena Blocker finding name the list, the records check accepts the job directory, and no replay.md is created (cargo test -p athena-core).
The typed replay field or record kind has a schema round-trip test and passes the records check (cargo test -p athena-data).
A pipeline test shows model call counts are equal for a run with a candidate rule change and a run without one, so the replay makes no model call (cargo test -p athena-core).

A test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs shows the verifier brief carries the replay summary (newly refused count, total, list) or 'no replay: <reason>', and stays within its size limit with a very long list (cargo test -p athena-context).
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the subcommand, the replay, the 10% hold, the typed record and the verifier brief summary.
git diff shows no change to athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows; the 10% threshold is a code constant; no existing reading rule changed; no replay.md is written.

out_of_scope: Detecting refusal-rule changes by a flag or by matching diffs
Creating a free-form replay.md in the job directory
Adding a switch to skip the replay
Automatic disk cleanup or disk reservation before the verifier (a separate job from the introspection)
departures: Large multi-crate change touching the run pipeline, a new record kind and a subcommand; well above the reference cost and time. Prior attempts failed in planning and on disk.
urgent_reason: It cuts failed or rejected attempts by trying a new refusal rule on real history before it lands.
hard_reason: It adds a hold rule to the run pipeline and gate that judges candidates, changes a records kind, and runs a replay at verification, so mistakes are costly.
